    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields

      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string

          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped
            from the national digits. The result must have 8 to 15 digits after
            the '+', and that E.164 string is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date

The requirement: when an owner is created, return `namesakeCount` = the number of *existing* owners (before this create) sharing the same `firstName` and `lastName`, compared case-insensitively.

I followed the existing pattern for on-create derived fields (`customerCode`, `householdId`), keeping each concern in its own small unit:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `namesakeCount` integer to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and it is documented on `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

3. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — marked `namesakeCount` as ignored when mapping from `OwnerFieldsDto` (it's a server-assigned field, exactly like `customerCode`/`householdId`); the reverse `toOwnerDto` maps it automatically.

The `isNew()` + `null` guards ensure it's computed once, at create, and never on update. Because the candidate isn't persisted yet, the query naturally excludes it, satisfying the "before this create" semantics.

6. **Schema files** (h2/hsqldb/mysql/postgres) — added the `namesake_count` column, consistent with how `household_id` etc. were rolled out.
